title.noTraps: No traps are on. Turn on at least one service to learn when something probes your network.
title.week_one: Traps were hit {{count}} time in 7 days, last {{when}} from {{src}}
title.week_other: Traps were hit {{count}} times in 7 days, last {{when}} from {{src}}
title.quiet: No trap was hit in the last 7 days
title.failed: A trap is on, but the box could not set up the decoy. Nothing is listening.

meta: Updated {{time}}. Traps only listen and log. They do not block or hit back.
needAdmin: Only administrators can change the secondary IP or switch traps. Operators can still view and test traps.

conflict.title: Secondary IP {{ip}} clashes with a real device
conflict.body: Device {{name}} already uses this address, so the trap cannot listen. Change the secondary IP to an unused address.

decoy.title: Decoy machine
decoy.description: The trap is a fake machine on {{lan}}. Nobody has a reason to connect to it, so every connection deserves a look.
decoy.ipHint: An unused address inside {{lan}}. Vedette rejects an address that matches a device in the inventory. To remove the decoy IP, turn all traps off, empty this field and save.
decoy.mac: The box gave this address the MAC address {{mac}}.
decoy.problem: The box could not set up the decoy: {{reason}}.
decoy.hostnameHint: Pick a name that looks like a real server, such as FILESRV-OLD. Up to 15 characters.

serviceHint.smb: Counted when a client opens the share or a file in it
serviceHint.rdp: Counted when a client sends an RDP connection request
serviceHint.ssh: Counted on every connection, even one that only reads the banner
serviceHint.mssql: Counted when a client tries to log in
serviceHint.http: Counted on GET /, the fake login page and refused methods

state.conflict: Error: IP clashes with a device

traps.title: Traps by service
traps.description: Turn on each service so the decoy opens the matching port. A trap records what its service can see, listed under each service. A bare TCP connect that sends nothing is not recorded for SMB or MSSQL.
traps.caption: Traps and their status
traps.needIpReason: Set the decoy's secondary IP before turning a trap on
traps.testOffReason: Turn this trap on before testing
traps.testToast: Recorded a test hit on the {{service}} trap
traps.testNote: Test a trap to confirm it records hits. The test comes from the Vedette box itself, is labelled as a test, is not counted as a hit and sends no alert.
traps.testConflictReason: The secondary IP clashes with a real device. Change the secondary IP before testing.

exclusion.title: Vedette's own scanner does not count as a trap hit
exclusion.description: When Vedette scans for vulnerabilities or inventories actively, the box knocks on every port, traps included. To avoid false alarms, connections from the box are always ignored.
exclusion.whyBody: This is your own scanner. Without the exclusion every scan would raise a false alert.

hits.title: Trap hits
hits.description: Newest first. Includes decoy connections, honey token use and port scans across the decoys. Select a time to see the hour of events around the hit.
hits.caption: Trap hits
hits.filter: Filter by service, IP or device
hits.emptyBody: That is good news. Turn a trap on, then select Test trap to confirm it records hits.
hits.emptyBodyOff: No trap is on yet, so there is nothing to record. Follow the steps above, then select Test trap to see that the trap is recording.
hits.respondLabel: Respond to the hit from {{src}} at {{time}}

hit.titleTest: Test hit on the {{service}} trap at {{time}}
hit.noDevice: This IP is not in the inventory. It may be an unknown device that just joined the network.
hit.sessionHint: Content sent by the connecting machine. Treat it as untrusted data.
hit.events: Events in the {{minutes}} minutes around the hit
hit.eventsHint: Firewall, DHCP, AD and trap events about the source machine. Rows tagged Trap come from the trap.
hit.next1: Ask the user of {{src}} whether they are browsing network folders or running a scanning tool.
hit.next2: If they do not know, unplug the machine from the network and check for unknown software and running processes.
hit.next3: Compare the firewall events after the hit: did this machine connect to any other server?
hit.meta_scan: A sweep touched the decoy IPs: {{ip}}.

device.title: Internal trap hits
device.description: Times this device connected to a trap. A normal machine has no reason to.
device.none: This device has not hit any trap.

start.title: Get started with internal traps in three steps
start.step1: Give the decoy machine a secondary IP: an address in {{lan}} that no device uses, plus a decoy name, then select Save.
start.step2: Turn on each trap service in the table below.
start.step3: Select Test trap to make sure the trap is recording. From then on every connection to the decoy shows up here.

lanUnknown: your LAN (add it first under Devices, Scope and sensors)

personality.title: Decoy personalities
personality.description: Choose what each trap looks like to someone scanning the network. A decoy that matches a device you really have blends in. These decoys are in addition to the decoy machine above.
personality.suggestItem_one: You have {{count}} {{type}} ({{names}}), so an attacker expects to find one.
personality.suggestItem_other: You have {{count}} {{type}} devices ({{names}}), so an attacker expects to find them.

form.name: Decoy name
form.ipHintUnchecked: Not checked: no devices discovered yet, so Vedette cannot tell whether these are free: {{ips}}
form.ipHintNone: An unused address in your LAN.

personality.none: No extra decoys yet. Add one on a spare IP. Several decoys on different IPs also let Vedette spot a scan.

scan.title: Scan detection
scan.body: A device that touches two or more decoy IPs, or many ports on one decoy, within a minute raises one high-confidence alert that names the source device. Normal machines have no reason to do this.
scan.needDecoys: Add a decoy first. Detection needs at least two decoy IPs.

token.title: Honey tokens
token.description: Bait you plant on real systems. Nobody has a reason to use it, so any use is an alert that names where it came from. Plant a few in places an intruder would look.

what.file: A .docx or .xlsx for a file share. It calls home when opened.
what.credential: A user and password for a password manager or a script. Any login attempt with them alerts.
what.url: A web link. Opening it alerts.

nameHint.credential: Looks like an old service account: svc-backup-old.
nameHint.url: Names this token in alerts, for example Wiki admin link.
nameHint.dns: Names this token in alerts, for example Backup script host.

plantHint.credential: For example the IT password manager
plantHint.url: For example an intranet wiki page
plantHint.dns: For example a backup script config

token.emptyBody: Create one above, then plant it where an intruder would look first.

trigger.file: someone opens the file in Word or Excel and it loads a hidden image from the box.
trigger.credential: anyone tries to sign in with this user name, from any machine.
trigger.url: anyone opens the link in a browser or a link scanner fetches it.
trigger.dns: any machine looks the name up, for example a script or a malware config using it.

how.file: Download {{value}} from this page and copy it to the share. In this preview there is no download: the real box generates the file with its call-home address inside, and you copy it to the share like any other document.
how.credential: Save the user and password as an entry in a password manager or a script config. Do not create the account in Active Directory: the box alerts on the failed login.
how.url: Paste the link into a wiki page, a document or a note where an intruder reads about admin systems.
how.dns: Use {{value}} as a server name in a config or script. Forward the vedette.internal zone to the box in your DNS server so lookups reach it.

notHere.title: Traps need the appliance install
notHere.body: This is a container-only install: there is no vedette-host to run the honeypot container and its decoy address, so no trap can listen here and nothing on this page would be covered. Use the appliance install to run traps.
notHere.modules: Turn the module off in Settings, Modules

coverage.title: Is this enough?
coverage.description: A guide to which common attacker moves traps and tokens can see. It is not a score.
coverage.notListening: No trap is listening yet, so the traps and tokens see none of these moves. Turn a trap on and check that its status says Listening.

lateral.how: SMB decoys and decoy files on shares catch someone browsing for data.

credentials.how: Fake credentials alert on any login attempt. Real accounts that were stolen are not seen.

scanning.how: A sweep across the decoy IPs raises one alert that names the source.

documents.how: Decoy files, URL tokens and DNS tokens alert when touched.

outbound.how: Not a trap job: the Logs page matches SPAN metadata and syslog against the threat lists.

endpoint.move: Malware or tools running on a computer
endpoint.how: Traps do not watch what happens on endpoints. Use endpoint protection for that.

email.how: Traps and tokens do not see email. Use your mail provider's protection.

coverage.note: Traps catch an intruder who is already inside and touches something. They do not stop a break-in. More varied bait in more places gives better odds.
